column1: # What a workflow token actually reached, measured on GitHub Actions rather
# than read off a documentation page.
# Produced by pushing a workflow to a scratch branch of
# committed-nightly/ungranted with one job per permissions: block, each job
# running the same list of GET requests with the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN, and
# reading the status codes back out of the run log. The repository was flipped
# to private for the run, because on a public repository almost all of these
# succeed with no token at all and the measurement says nothing (see the README
# A `-` means that block was not measured for that path. The empty-block job
# of the first run could not run at all: on a private repository
# actions/checkout needs contents: read, and under `permissions: {}` the clone
# fails with "repository not found" before any step. The third run is the same
# list with no checkout step, which is the only way to see a metadata-only
# token, and it covers the paths where metadata was the open question.
# Columns are the HTTP status for a GET under each block. `metadata` is
# `permissions: {}`, which the runner resolves to exactly `Metadata: read`.
